summary: Events desk (EVT), 16 Oct 2026, D-11. 27 findings dated 3-16 Oct, plus exchange prices pulled from the Polymarket and Kalshi APIs at 13:44 UTC on 16 Oct. Surplus agreements. On deadline day the signed set is exactly the model's five pairs: Likud-RZP-Zehut, Together-Yisrael Beytenu, Yashar-Democrats, Shas-UTJ and Ra'am-Joint List. Otzma runs without a pact after Ben-Gvir's 13 Oct refusal of Amcha. Blue and White refused every pact, and Hendel declined Winter. SURPLUS_PAIRS needs no change; the CEC's own notice was not reachable. Lists. No list withdrew. Amcha lost its No. 8 under an organised Likud-RZP pressure campaign, and Winter vowed to run to the end. Its seat price on Polymarket fell from 0.645 to 0.225, matching the model's 0.245. Gantz repeated that he runs to the end, so the 0.25 withdrawal prior is stale (suggest 0.15). Gur Hasidism (about 30,000 voters) had not told its people to vote UTJ, a one-sided UTJ risk of about 0.6 seats. Coalition signals. Every change-bloc leader is now on record refusing to sit with Netanyahu: Bennett after an 11 Oct gaffe, Eisenkot, Lapid, Golan and Liberman. Liberman also ruled out any minority government, 'including ... for a transitional period', which cuts the basis for liberman_minority_ok 0.25 (suggest 0.12). Deri made a draft-exemption law the condition for any government Shas joins; haredi sources say both parties may recommend nobody. Winter recommends Netanyahu but ruled out any change-bloc-led government, which supports the Eisenkot floor and argues for amcha_center about 0.20. Hendel stays outside both blocs, so ZIONIST_ONLY holds. Herzog vowed to avoid a repeat election; a report that he pushed a Netanyahu-Eisenkot unity was denied. Events. The 7 Oct anniversary revelations moved no poll. Kan had the coalition up 2. Trump withheld an endorsement and ruled out a US strike on Iran before 3 Nov; the IDF raised its alert level. Markets price an Israel-Iran exchange by 31 Oct at about 15% and a postponement at about 6%. That hazard supports scaling EVENT_RISK to about 1.02-1.06, not 1.2. Markets. Kalshi's count-of-elections contract prices a repeat election at about 0.245 against the model's 0.251, which validates the post-deadlock stage and supersedes COA-F09's 3-15%. Bloc majorities also match (Kalshi NB 0.115 and change 0.105 vs model 0.136 and 0.078). Three things contradict the model. (1) Given that a government forms, markets give Eisenkot about 0.48 and Netanyahu about 0.30; the model gives 0.34 and 0.45 through a 0.213 'change-bloc defector' outcome that the anti-pacts do not support. (2) Threshold odds: polls and both exchanges put RZP-Zehut, Otzma and Ra'am at 0.88-0.99 and the Reservists at about 0.45, against the model's 0.56, 0.78, 0.76 and 0.21. The gap is the trailing-Likud geometry, a declared bet with a 2015/2019a record. (3) Polymarket's deepest party market makes Yashar the favourite for first place (0.665); the model favours Likud (0.60).

findings.claim: On deadline day (Friday 16 Oct, D-11) the surplus-vote map is exactly the model's five pairs. Signed: Likud with RZP-Zehut, Together with Yisrael Beytenu, Yashar with the Democrats, Shas with UTJ, and Ra'am with the Joint List. Three lists near the threshold have no pact. Otzma has none: Ben-Gvir refused Amcha on 13 Oct, and Likud had already signed with RZP-Zehut. Blue and White says it will sign with no list in either bloc. The Reservists have none, because Hendel would not sign with Winter.
findings.quant: Kikar HaShabbat, 16 Oct 2026 13:13 ('11 days to the election'; it calls the 16 Oct notice deadline 'today'): five signed pacts listed; it says a pact matters only if both lists pass. Ben-Gvir, 13 Oct (ToI 8:23 pm): 'Winter is Bennett 2, and therefore Otzma Yehudit will not sign a surplus-vote agreement with him.' Otzma was polling about 6 seats and Amcha was near 3.25%. Agudat Yisrael CEC member Avraham Yostmann (Kikar): Ben-Gvir's refusal 'may prove to be colossal stupidity'. Blue and White (Kikar): it will not sign with any party in either bloc.

findings.claim: Amcha Yisrael's No. 8, Davidi Ben Zion, quit the list on 13 Oct, citing the risk of missing the threshold. Netanyahu and Smotrich publicly urged the rest of the list, and Winter himself, to withdraw. N12 describes an organised pressure campaign: billboards near candidates' homes and job offers to candidates who step aside. The same campaign tested whether Noam could be talked out of the race. Winter vowed on 14 Oct to run to the end, and Noam says it will too.
findings.quant: JPost 14 Oct: Ben Zion, 'I am not prepared to let the votes of people who believed in this path go to waste.' Netanyahu: 'I call on the other members of the list to act similarly.' Smotrich called on Winter to 'announce his withdrawal'. N12/mako 14 Oct: billboard 'Dudi, withdraw! Don't endanger the country'; job placements offered; feelers to Rabbi Tau's circle on Noam. Winter, 14 Oct (ToI liveblog 4:53 pm): 'We will not give in... We will run to the finish with all our strength.'

findings.claim: Blue and White is staying in. Gantz said on 10 Oct he is 'staying in the race until the end' and needs no one's permission. On 16 Oct the party refused any surplus pact with either bloc. Gantz's pitch is a unity government that includes Netanyahu if he passes the threshold. It has polled 0 seats in every October poll, and markets give it a 5-9% chance of a seat.

Kikar 16 Oct: no surplus pact with either bloc. polls.csv 1-15 Oct: 0 seats in 16 of 16 polls that list it (Lazar 15 Oct: 1.1%). Polymarket seat 0.047 (bid 0.024, ask 0.069); Kalshi 0.085 (0.05/0.12). Model p_pass 0.011; blue_white_folds 0.25.

findings.claim: Gur, the largest Hasidic court (about 25,000-30,000 voters, roughly two-thirds of a seat), had issued no instruction to vote UTJ as of 14 Oct. Its activists were ordered not to campaign. The aim, per a Gur source, is to keep Belz's Eliakim Stark (UTJ No. 6) out of the Knesset after the Porush-Stark split from Agudat Yisrael. i24 reports a fallback of a quiet instruction to vote Code Black. Insiders expect a compromise, and Emess notes that instructions usually come about 1.5 weeks before polling day.
findings.quant: INN 14 Oct 22:22: 'At present there is an instruction not to conduct any activity toward the elections'; 'The goal... is to do everything to keep Stark out'. Some in Gur hope it costs UTJ two seats. Belz sources: Gur has 25,000-30,000 voters against UTJ natural growth of about 55,000. Kipa 14 Oct: Gur strength 'about thirty thousand votes'. i24 (Wednesday 14 Oct): Gur strength 'about one seat'; fallback 'a quiet instruction will pass to vote for the Black Color party'. Model: UTJ mean 8.8 (p05-p95 6-11); Code Black p_pass 0.016.

source.title: The threat of Gur Hasidism (Hebrew)

findings.model_link: UTJ share and the haredi family shock in bayes_model.project; LOYAL_SD utj 1.3. This is a one-sided downside tail.

findings.claim: On 15 Oct Liberman ruled out supporting any minority government, 'including a minority government for a transitional period'. He repeated that Yisrael Beytenu will not sit with Likud while Netanyahu leads it, and he demanded an all-Zionist coalition: 'No Ra'am, no Joint List, no Shas, and no United Torah Judaism.' He left one door open: 'Likud without Netanyahu can be a significant partner.'
findings.quant: JPost 15 Oct 18:25: 'We will not support any minority government, including a minority government for a transitional period.' No Likud with Netanyahu 'under any circumstances'. 'Likud without Netanyahu can be a significant partner.' 'No Ra'am, no Joint List, no Shas, and no United Torah Judaism.' He claims some Likud MKs may join a Zionist coalition. YB polls 9-10 seats.

source.title: Avigdor Liberman rules out minority government, Benjamin Netanyahu coalition

findings.model_link: BEHAVIOR['liberman_minority_ok'] = 0.25 (NEFF 14). The code comment rests on 'his own 2020 abstention precedent'. This pledge names and closes the transitional-minority route that the 2020 softening used. Suggest 0.25 -> 0.12 (NEFF 20). BEHAVIOR['liberman_haredi_ok'] = 0.20 is reaffirmed (hold, or 0.15). likud_sans_bibi: Liberman's door to a Likud without Netanyahu is open, which is consistent with the unity gate; the binding constraint stays inside Likud.
findings.site_use: Liberman has ruled out backing any minority government, even a transitional one (15 Oct).

findings.claim: On 15-16 Oct Liberman accused Eisenkot ('Gantz II') of building Yashar's lead in order to negotiate a government with Netanyahu. Eisenkot's public line is the opposite. On 12 Oct he said Netanyahu 'cannot serve as prime minister, minister or deputy minister'. On 16 Oct he said the 'leadership of October 7' must not stay 'for even one more day', and that the goal is more than 61 Zionist seats for the change bloc.
findings.quant: JPost 16 Oct (updated 14:24): Liberman says Eisenkot's campaign 'is not intended to shift a single vote from the draft dodgers bloc' and aims to out-poll Likud and then negotiate with Netanyahu. Eisenkot: 'We are 11 days away from the most fateful elections since the founding of the state.' Gantz on Liberman: 'hasn't done ten percent of what Gadi Eisenkot and I have done.' ToI liveblog 16 Oct 3:01 pm: Eisenkot targets a majority of 61+ Zionist seats. Ynet (12 Oct): Netanyahu 'cannot serve as prime minister, minister or deputy minister'.

findings.claim: On 11 Oct Bennett said Netanyahu could serve as a minister if he accepted the opposition's 'core tenets', including a state commission of inquiry. Within hours he called the remark ironic: 'We will not sit with him in any formation.' Eisenkot, Liberman ('Come hell or high water, we will not sit in a government with Netanyahu'), Lapid ('We will not cooperate with this') and Golan (asked for written pledges) closed ranks. All four change-bloc lists are now publicly anti-pact with Netanyahu.
findings.quant: ToI 12 Oct 2:51 am (remarks at the HaDor conference on Sunday 11 Oct): Bennett walk-back, 'Anyone who watched my remarks today understood that they were intended to illustrate the absurdity... We will not sit with him in any formation.' Eisenkot: 'Everyone who was in office [on October 7] is unfit to serve in command and leadership roles.' Liberman on X: 'Come hell or high water, we will not sit in a government with Netanyahu.' ToI 12 Oct 3:22 pm: Lapid hopes Herzog 'will not try to push for another fake unity government'; Golan urges written pledges.

findings.claim: President Herzog said on 12 Oct he will 'really, truly' do all he can to avoid repeat elections. 'Elections are not a civil war,' he said, adding that everyone will likely accept the results. The same day Ynet reported, from Yashar sources, that he had floated a Netanyahu-Eisenkot unity government. The President's Office replied: 'We categorically deny the report.' Lapid and Golan rejected any unity government with Netanyahu.
findings.quant: ToI 12 Oct 3:22 pm (Yedioth conference): 'do everything I can to establish a stable government for Israel'; 'really, truly will do all I can so there won't be repeat elections'; avoid 'going back to this again and again and again'. Ynet: President's Office, 'We categorically deny the report. The president has not discussed a unity government with any candidate or Knesset member.' Golan: 'There will be no unity government with Netanyahu.' Gantz: without unity the sides 'will bring upon us the next October 7'. ToI liveblog 15 Oct 11:40: Herzog in Baku, 'Elections are not a civil war.'

source.title: Herzog: I'll work to set up 'stable' government, Israel must avoid repeat elections

findings.model_link: likud_sans_bibi 0.125 (the code: 'Herzog's plea-deal / unity push is a tripwire, not a prior'). The tripwire has NOT fired: the report is denied and every change leader refuses Netanyahu. Herzog's stated aim backs the post-deadlock stage's premise that the formateur works to avoid a repeat; it does not back a higher unity gate.
findings.site_use: President Herzog has said he will do everything he can to avoid a repeat election (12 Oct).
findings.verification: opened (ToI article and Ynet report)

findings.claim: Haredi signals harden around the draft law. On 13 Oct JPost quoted haredi sources: Shas and UTJ may recommend neither Netanyahu nor Eisenkot, and may sit in opposition until a draft settlement survives judicial review. They are 'not expected' to help topple Netanyahu. On 14 Oct Deri made exemption the first condition: no government 'that Shas supports or participates in' without settling yeshiva students' status. Military Police draft-evader arrests resumed on 8 Oct, with crowds blocking arrests in Dimona and Bat Yam.
findings.quant: JPost 13 Oct (11:50, updated 19:10): 'neither party is inclined to recommend a candidate to the president after the election'. One idea is a government formed without the haredim that brings them in after a law passes. Deri, 14 Oct (Kikar interview via N12/mako 11:10): 'לא תהיה ממשלה בישראל שש"ס תומכת או משתתפת בלי שנסדיר את מעמד תלמידי הישיבות' ('There will be no government in Israel that Shas supports or participates in unless we settle the status of yeshiva students'). INN 8 Oct: Dimona and Bat Yam arrests thwarted by 'dozens' after a 'Color Black' alert.

source.title: Israeli election: Haredi parties may refuse to endorse both Benjamin Netanyahu, Gadi Eisenkot

findings.model_link: shas_defects 0.10, utj_defects 0.15 (supported: Eisenkot, Bennett and Liberman all campaign against exemption, so a defection deal has no policy space). NB_CORE treats haredi entry into a Netanyahu government as certain when NB>=61. Deri's condition is one Netanyahu has tried to meet, but the 'recommend nobody' reports back COA's 0.9-0.95. There is no formateur stage: who gets the first mandate is not modelled.
findings.site_use: Shas and UTJ condition any government on a draft-exemption law and may recommend no one to the President.

findings.claim: Winter's two-sided stance is now public and acrimonious, and the model's Eisenkot floor holds. On 12 Oct he ruled out joining any government led by the opposition bloc: 'זה לא יקרה בשום מצב' ('It won't happen under any circumstances'). His reason: 'Gadi is left, with Yair Golan and the Arabs - that is not an option for me.' He still says he will recommend Netanyahu. He also says Netanyahu is 'shooting us in the back' and can 'take a hike' if he prefers the haredim. Netanyahu, 16 Oct: 'Don't vote for Winter.'
findings.quant: Srugim 12 Oct (Ynet/Yedioth 'People of the State' conference): Winter rejects a mandate going to a change-bloc politician or a coalition led by Liberman or Eisenkot. Quote: 'גדי (איזנקוט) הוא שמאל, עם יאיר גולן והערבים - זו לא אופציה בשבילי' ('Gadi [Eisenkot] is left; with Yair Golan and the Arabs, that is not an option for me'). ToI (French) 12 Oct 20:16: Netanyahu is 'responsible for the collapse of the right'; 'il nous tire dans le dos' ('he is shooting us in the back'). JPost 16 Oct 12:46: Winter will recommend Netanyahu and will not join a government where the haredim hold the balance without a conscription law. CONFLICT: the same JPost piece says Winter 'did not rule out joining an Eisenkot or Liberman government', which contradicts Srugim's direct quote.

Bennett is not named, but 'not Liberman' implies little room. Suggest 0.30 -> 0.20. amcha_right = 0.60 (P joins): the recommendation pledge is reiterated, but the Netanyahu-Winter feud deepened. Hold 0.55-0.60. Moot in 75% of draws, where Amcha fails.

On 8 Oct he said: 'We are not in the bloc of Netanyahu and the haredim... and we are not in the bloc of Eisenkot and the Arab parties.' Of a grand coalition he said: 'If Netanyahu, Eisenkot and Bennett sit together, it's clear I'll be part of it.' Winter rejected his Zionist-only pact. Headline quote: 'אם נתניהו, איזנקוט ובנט יישבו ביחד, ברור שאהיה חלק' ('If Netanyahu, Eisenkot and Bennett sit together, it's clear I'll be part of it'). JPost 8 Oct: Hendel to Winter, 'Together, we will be a blocking bloc against non-Zionist governments and coalitions with haredi or Arab parties.' findings.claim: Eisenkot is openly planning for a minority government that would pass if the Arab parties abstain. He argues that the leader of the change list with the most votes should be the bloc's PM candidate, but the four change parties have not agreed a selection rule. He has warned Netanyahu that a caretaker strategy ('winning by losing') 'will not happen'. Opposition planning reported on 13 Oct goes further: replace Speaker Ohana and legislate before a government is sworn in.
findings.quant: JPost 16 Oct (Keinon): Eisenkot is 'considering a minority government that could pass a Knesset vote if the Arab parties abstain'; 'the leader of the party with the most votes should be the bloc's prime ministerial candidate'; the four change-bloc parties 'have not agreed on how to choose'. JPost 13 Oct: plans to replace the Speaker, set up the House and Constitution committees, and pass a state commission of inquiry and a two-term PM limit before a government; options include a minority government backed externally by Ra'am.

findings.claim: Voters prefer a unity government to a repeat election, but on partisan terms. In Lazar/Maariv (fieldwork 14-15 Oct, n=700) a majority prefer unity if the vote is inconclusive and 27% prefer another election (18% unsure). Nearly 40% of coalition voters want unity led by Netanyahu (32% prefer a new election). 54% of opposition voters accept unity only under their own bloc's leader. PM suitability: Eisenkot 48, Netanyahu 41.
findings.quant: JPost 16 Oct 08:43 (Maariv/Lazar-Panel4All, 14-15 Oct, n=700): 27% another election, 18% unsure, so about 55% prefer unity. Coalition voters: nearly 40% Netanyahu-led unity, 32% repeat. Opposition voters: 54% unity only under their leader. Head-to-heads: Eisenkot 48-41 Netanyahu; Bennett 43-43; Netanyahu 43-37 Liberman. Seats: Coalition 51, Opposition 51, Reservists 4, Arab lists 14.

source.authors: Jerusalem Post staff (Maariv / Lazar Research poll)

findings.claim: The October 7 anniversary brought a new wave of reports on what Netanyahu knew beforehand. Haaretz ran a book excerpt on a UAE warning; The Atlantic and WSJ reported an Egyptian warning; a 15 Oct Channel 12 report said Netanyahu passed up targeting Hamas leaders. 75% of Israelis back a state commission of inquiry. No anti-Netanyahu poll move followed. Kan/Kantar of 11 Oct had the coalition up 2 to 53 and the Eisenkot bloc down 2 to 50.
findings.quant: Irish Times 7 Oct: claims of a UAE and an Egyptian warning; Gallant says Netanyahu never told him; Netanyahu calls it 'fake news'; INSS survey 75% back a state commission. ToI liveblog 15 Oct 9:16 pm headline: 'Report says Netanyahu opted against targeting Hamas leaders weeks before Oct. 7.' Haaretz 11 Oct (Kan/Kantar, n=552): Eisenkot bloc 50 (-2), coalition 53 (+2), Arab lists 13, Reservists 4; Likud 20 (-1), Yashar 22 (-1); PM suitability Eisenkot 43, Netanyahu 38. Polymarket 'Likud wins most seats': 0.415 (1 Oct) -> 0.545 (4 Oct) -> 0.495 (7 Oct) -> 0.345 (16 Oct), a reversal driven by the 13-16 Oct polls, not by the revelations.

findings.claim: Security risk before polling day is elevated but priced as unlikely. On 8 Oct Trump posted that the US would not attack Iran before the 3 Nov midterms. Channel 12 reported that IDF chief Zamir had warned US counterparts that a strike could force the 27 Oct election to be postponed. Kan reported on 15 Oct that the IDF raised its alert level while having no concrete information of an Iranian or Hezbollah attack. Markets put an Israel-Iran strike exchange by 31 Oct at about 15% and a postponement at about 6%.
findings.quant: Trump (ToI 9 Oct): 'We will not be attacking Iran at any time prior to the midterm elections to be held in the United States on November 3rd.' INN 15 Oct 20:28 (citing Kan): 'no concrete information indicating that Iran or Hezbollah intends to attack'; 'We are acting to ensure that we are not caught by surprise.' Polymarket 'Israel x Iran ceasefire continues through' ($35.6m): 18 Oct 0.959, 21 Oct 0.935, 31 Oct 0.845, so P(qualifying strike) is about 0.04 / 0.065 / 0.155. Polymarket 'Will Israel election happen as scheduled?' 0.9375 (0.93/0.945; $62k).

source.title: Trump says US won't hit Iran this month, as Zamir said to warn strike could delay Israel's election

findings.model_link: EVENT_RISK = 1.2 (bloc-swing multiplier). The market hazard to polling day (about 0.08-0.10 by 27 Oct, interpolated) matches DYN-F24's 0.008/day x 11 days (about 0.09). Most such events moved the bloc by 1-2 seats (DYN-F24), so the multiplier at D-11 belongs at about 1.02-1.06, not 1.2. Separately, the model conditions on polling on 27 Oct, and the ~6% postponement risk is not represented anywhere.
findings.site_use: Election-day risk from an Iran or Hezbollah flare-up is priced at roughly one in ten; it widens the bloc swing slightly.
findings.verification: opened (ToI; INN flash 695457); market data from the Polymarket API

challenges.title: The 'Netanyahu + a change-bloc defector' outcome (0.213) contradicts the 12-16 Oct anti-pacts and both exchanges
challenges.what_literature_says: Every change-bloc leader made a categorical, dated public refusal to sit with Netanyahu: Eisenkot ('cannot serve as prime minister, minister or deputy minister', 12 Oct; 'not for even one more day', 16 Oct), Bennett ('We will not sit with him in any formation', 11-12 Oct), Lapid ('We will not cooperate', 12 Oct), Liberman ('under any circumstances', 15 Oct) and Golan (written pledges). In the comparative record only 1 of 220 cabinets contained parties that had publicly refused each other (COA-F02). The 2020 precedent the gate was graded on (Gantz) is carried this cycle by Blue and White, which has p_pass 0.011. Kalshi: Likud in the next government 0.345 vs model 0.475. PM conditional on formation: Netanyahu 0.30 vs model 0.45.
challenges.current_model: BEHAVIOR['centre_defects'] = 0.12 (NEFF 25), raised by the gap logistic. Under POST_DEADLOCK_STAGE the gates are resampled until one fires, so in deadlocks the defector branch takes a large share: government_formation.csv (16 Oct) gives 0.213, and Netanyahu PM 0.335.
challenges.proposed_change: Lower centre_defects to 0.05 (NEFF 30), the anti-pact rate with a margin for the Liberman-alleged Yashar path. Alternatively cap its share inside the post-deadlock resampling, so that a deadlock resolves mostly through unity, haredi entry, Ra'am entry or the minority branch in proportion to their own priors rather than through the first gate to fire. Report the PM table conditional on formation next to Kalshi.
challenges.how_to_test: validate_formation.py log score on 2019a/2019s/2020/2021 with centre_defects at 0.12, 0.08 and 0.05 (the 2020 realisation must keep non-zero probability). Sensitivity row in government_sensitivity.csv; external check against Kalshi KXISRAELPM and KXISRAELGOVT.

challenges.proposed_change: 0.25 -> 0.12 (NEFF 20). A pledge is not a law (one softening in two tests), but it is now explicit on the very path he used in 2020.

challenges.title: EVENT_RISK 1.2 versus a market-priced hazard
challenges.what_literature_says: Polymarket prices an Israel-Iran strike exchange at about 0.065 by 21 Oct and 0.155 by 31 Oct, roughly 0.08-0.10 by polling day. That matches DYN-F24's 0.008/day hazard. In this cycle such events moved the Netanyahu bloc 1-2 seats and briefly. The October 7 revelations moved nothing measurable. A postponement is priced at about 6%.
challenges.current_model: EVENT_RISK = 1.2 constant (about 2.2 seats of extra bloc sd). The model does not represent postponement.
challenges.proposed_change: Scale EVENT_RISK by horizon as the DYN desk proposed (about 1.02-1.06 at D-11). Note on the site that the forecast is conditional on polling on 27 Oct, with a market-priced ~6% postponement risk.
challenges.how_to_test: DYN-F24 event study and the horizon harness (validate_horizon.py) at D-7/D-21.

challenges.title: Blue and White's withdrawal prior is stale
challenges.what_literature_says: On 10, 13 and 16 Oct Gantz said he is running to the end and refused any surplus pact, a costly signal. He offers unity with Netanyahu if he passes. 0 of 16 October polls give it a seat.
challenges.current_model: PRIORS['blue_white_folds'] = 0.25 (withdrawal routes votes to Yashar .60 / Together .25).
challenges.proposed_change: 0.25 -> 0.15, and collapse via RESOLVED on 23 Oct as planned. Watch the code's caution: the transfer moves Yashar's mean and can toggle TRAIL.
challenges.how_to_test: Registration-effects readout (registration_effects.csv) before and after; check the TRAIL switch.

challenges.title: A one-sided UTJ downside from Gur's missing vote instruction
challenges.what_literature_says: As of 14 Oct, Gur (25,000-30,000 voters, about 0.6-0.8 seats) had issued no instruction to vote UTJ and had frozen campaigning to keep Stark out. A Code Black diversion is mentioned. Insiders expect a late compromise.
challenges.current_model: UTJ has a symmetric haredi family shock (LOYAL_SD utj 1.3); there is no event for a sectoral sit-out.
challenges.proposed_change: If no Gur instruction is published by 23 Oct, add a UTJ-only downside event, probability 0.3, size -0.6 seat (half abstain, half to Code Black, which stays sub-threshold). Otherwise leave as is.
challenges.how_to_test: Evidence class: a Gur instruction in HaModia or Kikar/Bhol by 23 Oct. Post-election: UTJ's vote in Gur-heavy stations (Bnei Brak, Ashdod, Arad) in the kalpi panel.

open_questions: The CEC's official notice of registered surplus agreements for the 26th Knesset was not located: bechirot.gov.il returned an empty page to both fetch tools. Kikar (16 Oct) is the deadline-day source. Re-check the CEC/gov.il publication around 18-19 Oct before freezing SURPLUS_PAIRS.

Winter's stance on a Bennett-led government: Srugim's 12 Oct direct quote rules out any change-bloc-led government (Liberman and Eisenkot named), but JPost (16 Oct, Keinon) says he 'did not rule out joining an Eisenkot or Liberman government'. Locate the Channel 12 transcript.
Will Gur publish a vote instruction for UTJ, and when? Watch HaModia and the haredi sites up to 23 Oct; i24 mentions a quiet Code Black instruction as the fallback.
The legal last day for a list to withdraw before polling, relevant to Blue and White, Amcha and Noam, was not verified this round.

The Elector app: an undated i24 report says the CEC voted 19-11 to let parties report identified voters in real time, and an undated Ynetnews report says the High Court then banned the app. Dates and final status were not verified, and it bears on GOTV and turnout reporting.

Market liquidity: the threshold and bloc markets carry $5-18k of volume (Kalshi's count market about $600 on the '1' leg). Only the PM ($46.8m), Likud-largest ($886k) and Iran-ceasefire ($35.6m) markets are deep. Weight the comparisons accordingly.
Blue and White's claim (Kikar, 16 Oct) that Zelekha would join Netanyahu for the finance ministry is a rival's assertion; there is no statement from Zelekha.
Does the Lazar finding that about 40% of coalition voters prefer a Netanyahu-led unity government reflect Likud elites? No Likud figure has publicly floated a unity government without Netanyahu.
